reviews.review: The main storyline or 'the true path of the Tenno' is abseloutly insane. DE has pumped so much effort into the recent quests and for me it really means a lot. I have played Warframe since 19th Janurary 2016, I have gone on breaks but I just keep coming back to the game. It's loot farming nature helps take my mind off everything, it's a real treat for hard work. There is big range of unique weapons to take into battle, with different versions, for example, prime, wraith, vandal etc. I dont think I can stop playing unless I generally have nothing else to do. DE are pumping out new Warframes for you to try out really quickly and the ideas that make the Warframes comes from the amazing community. Warframe has a strong community, with it's monthly dev streams, prime time, the forums, clans and even the trading market. Alot of people see the game as 'pay to win' but what they dont realise is that you can do just as well if you don't buy platinum. So, if you are thinking of trying Warframe, do it - it's free! Have fun!

so the short version of this review is as follows:
as just an all around game this is a 4/10
as a FTP (free to play) game its an 8/10 or a 9/10
gameplays a little repetitive but otherwise fun 
strories meh 
lots of grinding 

heres the long version:

All free to play games have one sole aspect in common, no matter what genre or game it is if it's a free to play game it will have this feature. That feature of course is in game purchases. Some paid games have them but generally these purchases are not too prevalent, in FTP's however these purchases are at the forefront. Logistically this makes sense, a game has to make money somehow right, so the question becomes how many in game purchases is too many? and that's where warframe comes in.

Let me start by saying that warframe is probably the best FTP game that I've ever played on steam, it is one of the only games that i know of that has such an intricate combat system and grandios maps for the player to use/explore all for free. In and of itself that, for me atleast, takes this game to a 8/10 already. 

That being said the in game purchases take it back to a solid 4/10. If you want anything new, guns swords skins warframes etc. it can be purchased for the in game currency of platinum, however unlike alot of really bad free to plays this game offers another option. Instead of buying the actual equipment, you can buy the blueprint of the equipment; gather the necessary parts from different areas (certain resources are limited to certain planets but for the most part everythings eventually accessible)(there is however ALOT of grinding/farming to be done as is the case for most FTP's) and then combine them in your foundry. The one drawback of this is that everything and I mean EVERYTHING takes time.
Yes theres the time you take to find the resources or to save up the credits for the blueprint (some bosses also have a chance of dropping certain blueprints) but on top of that there are literal time requirements for every crafting item. this wouldn't be so  bad if we're talking achievable in a day at max but no; at minimum equipment is 6 hours, at maximum so far I've had 3 days, most of the equipment falls into the 12 hour category which isnt overkill but is still annoying. Of course you have the option to rush this process but thats done with, you guessed it, platinum. this becomes even more infuriating in the specific case of crafting a warframe. Instead of using hypotheticals I'll give you an actual example from my gameplay: on venus there's a boss called the jackal, after defeating him you have a 33% chance to be dropped the chasis of the warframe rhino, a 33% chance for the neuroptics of the rhino, and a 22% chance for the systems of the rhino, all three are required to craft the actual warframe the rhino. Now it took me 12 playthroughs of this mission for me to actually acquire all 3 parts, so about 2 hours give or take. Then after gathering all the parts I realized i didn't have enough plastids (a resource i had previously never seen) to craft the systems. So after looking up where to get plastids i found that I needed to go to the planet/moon phobos which was several missions away. after about another 3 hours of completing missions on mars (which unlocks phobos) and actual mission playing on phobos looking for plastids, I had enough. So 5 hours give or take to collect all the ingredients. Now I have to craft all 3, ONE GREAT ASPECT THIS GAME HAS OVER MOST FTP'S IS IT ALLOWS YOU TO CRAFT MULTIPLE THINGS AT ONCE, this cut my waiting time for each object down to 12 hours. Once those 3 were finished I'm able to assemble the rhino, which will take 3 days (all warframes I've seen so far take 3 days to craft). As I type this I still have 24 hours left to complete the crafting of this warframe. In total itll be about 90 hours of time just so I can get a SECOND warframe. The ingame purchases mainly come down to would you rather spend your time or your money, as they always do. There are other things you can do with the plat, for one you only get 12 base colors for your warframe all of which are god awful, and for some price of plat you can buy the rest of the colors in that pack, or one of the other 4 packs. Again this isn't saying i completely deplore this system, as this is a FTP so I understand it's neccesity, I just personally wish they'd toned it back a little.

My next problem is a smaller one, simply put if you have the ability to purchase something right off the bat (not plat but with credits earned in game) then you should be able to access the necessary ingredients. If the game gives me a sword blueprint I shouldn't have to progress 2 planets just to get the stuff for said blueprint. I'm going to leave it at that.

As far as the story goes the voice acting is bland and they reuse one boss 3 times in the first 6 main planets, so that should give you a good idea of what you're dealing with. 

All in all if you're looking for a game that costs no money and that you can enjoy thats not TF2 this is an ok choice. Just look at the wiki alot and try to sell stuff to other players at the bazaar.
